---
title: "Viewshed: What's Visible from Here"
date: 2026-09-07
categories: [tool, raster, bilingual]
description: "Given a DEM and an observer point, compute which cells are visible — accounting for terrain occlusion — and see it as a colored map. Runs on R; Python shown as reference only."
---

Elevation alone answers "how high." A viewshed answers a different
question: from one point on the terrain, looking outward, which other
points can you actually see? A hill in between blocks the view behind
it the same way a building would — this is exactly the computation
behind cell-tower placement, wind-turbine visual-impact studies, and
"does this property really have the panoramic view listed."

Every other article in this Raster family shows the same computation
running live in Python *and* R, side by side, agreeing on the answer.
This one doesn't — not because the idea changed, but because the
tooling did. Read on for why, and what it means for how this page is
built.

Just want the map, without the rest of the reading? Use the
[standalone tool](/tools/viewshed-calculator.html) — same engine,
click a point directly.

## 1. Upload your file

A `.tif`/`.tiff` digital elevation model (DEM) — one band of elevation
values.

## 2. Why viewshed, and what "visible" actually means here

Four things worth knowing before the first computed map:

- **It's occlusion, not distance.** A cell right next to the observer
  can be invisible (hidden behind a ridge two cells away) while a cell
  much farther off is perfectly visible across open ground. The
  algorithm traces the line of sight to every other cell and checks
  whether the terrain in between rises above that line anywhere along
  the way.
- **A working projection, not a correction.** `terra::viewshed()`
  requires projected (linear-unit) coordinates — it refuses geographic
  lon/lat data outright, and rightly so: the algorithm reasons in real
  distances and angles, which degrees can't give it directly. A
  geographic DEM (SRTM tiles, for instance, ship this way) is
  reprojected internally for the calculation, to a UTM zone picked
  from the raster's own centre. The **original file is never
  modified** — this is a working projection for the computation, not
  a claim that webGeoDS found "the correct CRS." A DEM spanning
  multiple UTM zones, sitting near the poles, or covering a very large
  area would need a deliberate projection choice instead — the
  automatic pick here is a reasonable default for a single local DEM,
  not a universal answer.
- **"Visible" means visible *under this terrain model*, not "a human
  would see it."** The result accounts for terrain height, observer
  and target height above ground, and a curvature/refraction
  coefficient (`terra::viewshed()`'s `curvcoef`, default ≈0.857) — it
  does not account for vegetation, buildings, or atmospheric haze. It
  answers "is the ground itself in the way," a real and useful
  question, just not the complete one.
- **The output is boolean, not a gradient.** Every other computed map
  in this Raster family (Band Math, NDVI) is a continuous value shown
  on a color ramp. A viewshed is yes/no per cell — visible cells are
  highlighted, everything else is left transparent so the base map
  shows through underneath.

## 3. Shared map and result

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
sharedMap = {
  const map = new window.WebGeoDS.Map({ center: [12.45, 41.9], zoom: 4, height: "480px" });
  await map.ready();
  return map;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sharedMapEl = sharedMap.element
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
FOOTPRINT_PAINT = ({
  "fill-color": "#42583c",
  "fill-opacity": 0.35,
  "fill-outline-color": "#2a2117"
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Both stops the same warm color -- a boolean result, not a gradient:
// any finite value (only ever 1, "visible") paints solid, NaN ("not
// visible") stays transparent via shared/map.js's existing NaN
// handling in _renderRasterCanvas — no changes needed there.
VIEWSHED_RAMP = [
  [0.00, 255, 213, 79],
  [1.00, 255, 213, 79]
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
  const binary = atob(base64Str);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable rResult = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
rCompute = WebGeoDS.getCellValue("viewshed-r", Generators)
{
  if (rCompute && rCompute.summary) {
    const s = rCompute.summary;
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("viewshed-r-footprint", rCompute.footprint, { paint: FOOTPRINT_PAINT });
    await sharedMap.fitToData(rCompute.footprint);
    await sharedMap.setRasterImage("viewshed-r-result", {
      bounds: s.wgs84Bounds,
      width: s.width,
      height: s.height,
      values: new Float32Array(base64ToBytes(s.data).buffer),
      min: 0,
      max: 1,
      colorRamp: VIEWSHED_RAMP
    });
    mutable rResult = s;
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
statCard = {
  const s = rResult;
  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";

  const row = (label, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = label;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s) {
    row("Result", "—");
    return box;
  }

  row("Dimensions", `${s.width} × ${s.height} px`);
  row("Original CRS", s.originalCrs ?? "—");
  row("Calculation CRS", s.calculationCrs);
  row("Observer height", `${s.observerHeight} m`);
  row("Visible pixels", s.visiblePixels.toLocaleString());
  row("Total pixels", s.totalPixels.toLocaleString());
  row("Visible %", `${s.visiblePercent}%`);

  return box;
}
```

## 4. Compute: viewshed in R — runnable here; Python — reference only

::: {.panel-tabset}

## R — runnable in this browser

```{.webgeods-r #viewshed-r}
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

if (is.null(path)) {
  # Synthetic hill DEM, deliberately in a GEOGRAPHIC CRS (EPSG:4326) --
  # the case terra::viewshed() itself refuses to compute on directly
  # (see section 2), so the fallback exercises the same reprojection
  # path a real geographic DEM would.
  n <- 20
  xs <- 0:(n - 1)
  ys <- 0:(n - 1)
  elevation_vals <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
  r <- rast(elevation_vals, crs = "EPSG:4326")
  ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)
} else {
  r <- rast(path)
}

elevation <- r[[1]]

observer_lon <- 12.45
observer_lat <- 41.90
observer_height <- 1.8

# Same missing-CRS convention as the rest of the Raster family, but
# here the stakes are higher than a display nuance: viewshed cannot
# pick a working projection or place an observer without knowing
# where on Earth the file actually is, so this refuses outright
# rather than silently assuming WGS84 (try the no-CRS example in
# section 6 to see this happen).
if (crs(elevation) == "") {
  stop("This file has no declared CRS — a real-world location is required to compute a viewshed (to choose a working projection and place the observer correctly). Upload a georeferenced DEM.")
}

original_crs_label <- {
  crs_desc <- crs(elevation, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(elevation, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

# Working/calculation CRS -- see section 2. The original raster (and
# original_crs_label above) is never modified.
if (is.lonlat(elevation)) {
  e <- ext(elevation)
  center_lon <- (e$xmin + e$xmax) / 2
  center_lat <- (e$ymin + e$ymax) / 2
  utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
  calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone
  elevation_calc <- project(elevation, paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg), method = "bilinear")
} else {
  elevation_calc <- elevation
}

calc_crs_label <- {
  crs_desc <- crs(elevation_calc, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(elevation_calc, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

# The observer arrives as lon/lat and is reprojected into the same
# calculation CRS the raster itself is in.
obs_pt <- vect(matrix(c(observer_lon, observer_lat), ncol = 2), crs = "EPSG:4326")
obs_pt_calc <- project(obs_pt, crs(elevation_calc))
obs_xy <- as.numeric(crds(obs_pt_calc)[1, ])

vs <- viewshed(elevation_calc, loc = obs_xy, observer = observer_height, target = 0)

# NaN renders transparent in shared/map.js's canvas renderer -- "not
# visible" becomes NaN instead of FALSE/0, so only the visible area
# paints, reusing the same renderer Band Math/NDVI already use
# unmodified.
vs_num <- as.numeric(values(vs, mat = FALSE))
visible_mask <- vs_num == 1
vs_num[!visible_mask] <- NaN
vs_num[visible_mask] <- 1

n_visible <- sum(visible_mask, na.rm = TRUE)
n_total <- length(vs_num)

e_calc <- ext(elevation_calc)
bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e_calc$xmin, " ", e_calc$ymin, ", ", e_calc$xmax, " ", e_calc$ymin, ", ",
  e_calc$xmax, " ", e_calc$ymax, ", ", e_calc$xmin, " ", e_calc$ymax, ", ",
  e_calc$xmin, " ", e_calc$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(elevation_calc))
bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))
e_wgs84 <- ext(bbox_wgs84)

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("viewshed footprint")),
    geometry = list(type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"), coordinates = list(footprint_coords))
  ))
)

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(vs_num, con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
data_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(vs)),
  height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(vs)),
  data = jsonlite::unbox(data_b64),
  wgs84Bounds = round(c(e_wgs84$xmin, e_wgs84$ymin, e_wgs84$xmax, e_wgs84$ymax), 6),
  originalCrs = jsonlite::unbox(original_crs_label),
  calculationCrs = jsonlite::unbox(calc_crs_label),
  observerHeight = jsonlite::unbox(observer_height),
  visiblePixels = jsonlite::unbox(n_visible),
  totalPixels = jsonlite::unbox(n_total),
  visiblePercent = jsonlite::unbox(round(100 * n_visible / n_total, 1))
)

result_out <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

## Python — reference (desktop/server)

::: {.callout-warning}
**Not runnable in this browser tool.** This is valid Python/GDAL —
the equivalent desktop/server workflow — shown for reference. See
[why](#why-python-is-reference-only-here) below.
:::

```python
from osgeo import gdal

# Reference implementation only -- not executable in this browser
# tool. Exact keyword names can vary slightly by GDAL version; this
# matches the GDAL 3.x osgeo.gdal.ViewshedGenerate() API.
src_ds = gdal.Open("dem.tif")
src_band = src_ds.GetRasterBand(1)

gdal.ViewshedGenerate(
    srcBand=src_band,
    driverName="GTiff",
    targetRasterName="viewshed.tif",
    creationOptions=[],
    observerX=500100.0,       # in the DEM's own (projected) CRS units
    observerY=4600100.0,
    observerHeight=1.8,
    targetHeight=0.0,
    visibleVal=1.0,
    invisibleVal=0.0,
    outOfRangeVal=0.0,
    noDataVal=-1.0,
    dfCurvCoeff=0.85714,       # same default terra::viewshed() uses
    mode=gdal.GVM_Edge,
    maxDistance=0.0,           # 0 = unlimited
)
```

:::

## 5. Why Python is reference-only here {#why-python-is-reference-only-here}

Every other article in this Raster family runs Python and R side by
side and confirms they agree on the numbers. This one can't, and it's
worth being precise about why rather than waving at "GDAL isn't
supported":

The GDAL Python bindings expose `ViewshedGenerate()`, which provides
the corresponding GDAL implementation — the same underlying algorithm
`terra::viewshed()` uses on the R side. However, GDAL is not available
in the curated Pyodide package index used by this browser runtime.
Attempting to load it returns `No known package with name 'gdal'` —
tested directly against this project, not assumed from general
knowledge. `rasterio` itself, this site's usual Python raster engine,
has never had a viewshed function of its own; it's a thin I/O layer
over GDAL, not an analysis library. No actively-maintained pure-Python
alternative exists either — the closest candidates
(`whitebox`/WhiteboxTools, `richdem`) are a standalone compiled
executable and a C++ extension respectively, neither usable inside
Pyodide.

The Python example above shows the equivalent desktop/server workflow
but is not executable in this browser tool.

The rest of this site's implicit promise has been "Python and R, side
by side." This article refines that to "Python and R, when the
browser runtime allows it" — a statement of what's actually true,
not an exception being quietly worked around. Forcing a from-scratch
numpy reimplementation just to keep two live panels would have traded
a real, tested algorithm for an untested one, on a page whose whole
point is trustworthy answers.

## 6. A DEM with no declared CRS

Unlike the rest of the Raster family, this isn't a cosmetic
"Unknown ⚠️" row — the R cell above refuses to compute at all on a
CRS-less file (`stop()`, not a graceful fallback), because a viewshed
genuinely cannot be placed on Earth without knowing where the file
already is. Click below to load a DEM with the CRS deliberately
omitted, then run the R cell in section 4 to see the refusal itself,
surfaced as a normal R error in the cell's output.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
loadNoCrsExampleButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.textContent = "📋 Load a no-CRS example";
  button.onclick = async () => {
    await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("viewshed-r")?.setCode(rNoCrsExampleCode);
    document.getElementById("viewshed-r")?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "center" });
  };
  return button;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rNoCrsExampleCode = `library(terra)

n <- 20
xs <- 0:(n - 1)
ys <- 0:(n - 1)
elevation_vals <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
# crs deliberately omitted -- the whole point of this example.
r <- rast(elevation_vals)
ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)

elevation <- r[[1]]

if (crs(elevation) == "") {
  stop("This file has no declared CRS — a real-world location is required to compute a viewshed (to choose a working projection and place the observer correctly). Upload a georeferenced DEM.")
}

"unreachable -- the stop() above always fires for this example"`
```
